info.name: MyExpense — Auth (1) + User & Settings (2) + Categories (3) + Transactions (4) + Statistics (§14) + Contacts & Groups (6.1/6.2) + Splits & Settle up (6.3/6.4) + Activities & Notifications (7) + Budget (5)
info.description:
Domain 1: all 8 endpoints of the auth domain (docs/api/authentication-api.md).
Domain 2: all 5 endpoints of the User & Settings domain (docs/api/api-overview.md §2) — requests 9 onwards.
Domain 3: all 5 endpoints of the Categories domain (docs/api/api-overview.md §3) — requests 19 onwards, with SUBCATEGORY coverage in requests 32-44 and ADR 0021 coverage (DELETE, the usage pre-flight, the protected Misc row and RENAME PROPAGATION) in requests 84-112.
Domain 4: all 5 endpoints of the Transactions domain (docs/api/api-overview.md §4) — requests 45 onwards.
Statistics: the ONE endpoint of docs/api/api-overview.md §14 — requests 75-83 (75-78 are a one-shot fixture, 79 is the roll-up proof).

NOTE — Statistics (requests 75-83, docs/decisions/0022-statistics-expenses-by-parent-category.md). Five things to know before running them:
  * REQUESTS 75-78 ARE A FIXTURE AND MUST BE RUN EXACTLY ONCE per account — running them twice doubles every amount, and requests 79/81 assert exact numbers. They write SEPTEMBER 2026 on purpose, because every Domain 4 request above writes OCTOBER 2026.
  * EXPENSES ONLY, STRUCTURALLY. There is NO `type` parameter on §14 and there never will be: income rows carry category_id = NULL, so they cannot join to a category, and the aggregating query contains no mention of `type` at all — there is no clause to weaken. An income breakdown is REJECTED, not deferred (income is not a category, so an income pie would be one 100% slice forever).
  * THE ROLL-UP IS THE WHOLE FEATURE (request 79). A parent's `amount` is INCLUSIVE of its subcategories, and `subcategories[]` carries each child's own amount. The parent's OWN direct spend is NOT a field — it is `amount` minus the sum of the children. `totalSpent` is exactly the sum of `categories[].amount`, with each child counted ONCE, because the total sums the parents.
  * PERCENTAGES ARE CLIENT-SIDE. There is no `percentage` field, no `transactionCount` field and no currency field on any amount.
  * ZERO SPEND IS A 200 (request 80) with `totalSpent: 0.00` and `categories: []` — never a 404, and zero-spend categories are OMITTED rather than returned as 0.00. The drill-down is the EXISTING `GET /transactions?categoryId=&dateFrom=&dateTo=`; there is deliberately no statistics drill-down endpoint.

RUN ORDER MATTERS for Domain 4: requests 45+ depend on `userId` (request 9), `foodCategoryId`/`transportCategoryId` (request 19) and `subcategoryId` (request 32). Run 1 → 2 → 9 → 19 → 32 first, or just run the whole collection in order against a brand-new account.

NOTE — Domain 4 (requests 45-74). The five things worth knowing before running them:
  * INCOME IS NOT A CATEGORY (ADR 0018). An income transaction carries category_id = NULL and the server fills categoryName 'Income' / categoryIconName 'cash-outline' / categoryGlyph 'I' / categoryTone 'success' from service/IncomeCategorySnapshot — constants written during Domain 3 that had NO consumer until now. Request 47 is their first exercise. Sending a categoryId with type 'income' is a 400, never a silently ignored field (request 46). categoryTone is derived from `type` alone: success for income, neutral for expense.
  * THE CATEGORY SNAPSHOT IS SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE, AND SINCE 2026-10-25 IT IS NO LONGER FROZEN FOREVER (ADR 0019 §5, amended by ADR 0021 §1). Five columns — category_name, parent_category_name, category_icon_name, category_glyph, category_tone — are copied at write time and no request body accepts any of them. ~~Renaming a category later must NOT rewrite transaction history~~ — REVERSED by Project Owner ruling: a rename (and an icon or glyph change) now PROPAGATES to that category's transactions, so the columns are frozen UNTIL THE CATEGORY ITSELF CHANGES. Any assertion that the OLD name survives a rename is inverted; requests 105-112 are the proof, and request 45's console notes carry the correction. What is unchanged: no READ path joins `categories` at all, categoryId holds THE LEAF (a subcategory id if one was chosen), categoryName is never a composed path, and category_tone follows `type` and propagates never.
  * THE categoryId FILTER ROLLS UP. Requests 50 and 51 are the pair that proves it: a TOP-LEVEL id matches transactions tagged to it AND to its subcategories, a subcategory id matches that subcategory alone. A categoryId filter never matches an income row (use type=income).
  * OPTIMISTIC CONCURRENCY. PATCH requires `version`; a stale one is 409 VERSION_CONFLICT (request 56). Note there are TWO 409s on that endpoint with OPPOSITE client behaviour — VERSION_CONFLICT means re-fetch and retry, RECEIPT_ALREADY_ATTACHED (request 69) must never be retried.
  * DELETE IS A SOFT DELETE. It sets deleted_at and removes nothing (constitution §14 — offline clients need deletes to propagate, not vanish), so the row stays in the table while disappearing from every read. A second DELETE is a 404, not a 204.

NOT IMPLEMENTED in Domain 4, deliberately: POST /receipts/upload-signature and `receiptSignedUrl` (the Cloudinary plan's signed-delivery support is unconfirmed and there are no credentials). The receiptPublicId FIELD and column ARE implemented, including the claim check — requests 68-70 exercise it with hand-made values, which is the only way to get one today. Nothing group- or split-related was implemented in Domain 4 itself; the group half has since landed — see the NOTE on requests 216-225 below.

Login and Refresh automatically save accessToken/refreshToken into collection variables, so later requests just work without copy-pasting. Every Domain 2/3 request sends 'Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}', so run '2. Login' first.

IMPORTANT for Domain 3: register a BRAND-NEW account before running requests 19+. The 8 default categories are seeded at registration, and accounts created before Domain 3 existed have none of the seven (V8 did backfill them a protected Misc row, so such an account now holds exactly one category).

NOTE — ADR 0021 (docs/decisions/0021-category-rename-propagates-and-misc-reassignment-on-delete.md, 2026-10-25) — requests 84-112, and it is COUPLED TO MIGRATION V8__categories_misc_fallback.sql: both halves must land in the same restart. Six things to know before running them:
  * THE SEED SET IS 8, NOT 7 — `Misc` (ellipsis-horizontal-outline, glyph M) is last, and it is the ONE row per user with isProtected: true. This is NOT `Income` coming back: the count moved 8 -> 7 -> 8 with different membership each time. Request 19 asserts all of it.
  * Misc IS FOUND BY THE isProtected FIELD, NEVER BY ITS NAME — in the service (WHERE user_id = :callerId AND is_protected, in exactly one method), in these tests, and in the client. A user may own their own category called `misc`, names are unique only case-insensitively, and a name-matched reassignment target would be hijackable by a rename.
  * DELETE /categories/{id} RETURNS 200 WITH A BODY, not 204 — { reassignedTransactionCount, deletedSubcategoryCount } — because this delete mutates rows the caller did not name. It is a HARD delete (categories has no deleted_at), it CASCADES to subcategories, and transactions tagged to those cascaded children go to Misc, NOT to the surviving parent. A second DELETE is 404 CATEGORY_NOT_FOUND, which a client retrying a confirmed delete must treat as SUCCESS.
  * GET /categories/{id}/usage IS THE PRE-FLIGHT, and it exists because a client must never derive a total from a PAGINATED list: counting from its own transactions store would miss a category with 300 transactions none of which are on the current page, and delete it with no warning at all. It rolls up (parent + children), it is side-effect-free, and it is LEGAL on Misc — only deleting Misc is refused.
  * A RENAME NOW PROPAGATES, IN TWO UPDATES. UPDATE 1 refreshes categoryName/categoryIconName/categoryGlyph on rows tagged to the renamed row itself. UPDATE 2 refreshes parentCategoryName ONLY, on rows tagged to its CHILDREN — the one that gets missed, because a transaction on `Food > Lunch` carries LUNCH s id, so renaming Food matches ZERO rows in UPDATE 1. An icon-only change must NOT trigger UPDATE 2 (there is no parent_category_icon_name column). updatedAt IS bumped; version is NOT; categoryTone never propagates; income rows (categoryId null) can match neither.
  * 400 CATEGORY_PROTECTED IS PER-FIELD, NOT PER-ROW. Deleting Misc and renaming Misc are both refused with that code (400, never 403 — the row exists and is the caller s). Its iconName, glyph and monthlyCap ARE editable, and an icon change on Misc propagates like any other.

NOTE — ADR 0018 (docs/decisions/0018-income-is-not-a-category.md, 2026-10-21) changed two things in Domain 3, both reflected below:
  * The seed set is 7, not 8 — 'Income' is GONE. *(Count superseded on 2026-10-25: it is 8 again, with `Misc` as the 8th — see the ADR 0021 note above. The membership and the reasoning in this bullet stand unchanged for those seven.)* Income is not a category: transactions.type is the discriminator, income rows carry category_id = NULL with the four display values supplied from the server's own constants (service/IncomeCategorySnapshot). Accounts registered BEFORE this change keep a stray 8th 'Income' row; re-register to see seven.
  * Category names are now unique CASE-INSENSITIVELY (migration V4__categories_case_insensitive_name.sql replaces uq_categories_user_id_name with the functional unique index uq_categories_user_id_lower_name). Request 21b asserts the inverted behaviour: lowercase 'pets' used to succeed alongside 'Pets' and now returns 409. The error code CATEGORY_NAME_ALREADY_EXISTS is unchanged.

NOTE — ADR 0019 (docs/decisions/0019-subcategories-one-optional-level.md, 2026-10-22) added ONE OPTIONAL LEVEL OF SUBCATEGORIES, and added NO endpoint. Requests 32-44 cover it. The four things to know before running them:
  * GET /categories now returns a TWO-LEVEL TREE. The root array holds TOP-LEVEL categories only; a subcategory appears solely inside its parent's `subcategories` array. CategoryResponse gained `parentCategoryId` and `subcategories`, both always present (so `subcategories` is [] and never null), and on 2026-10-25 it gained `isProtected` as well. Purely additive — for an account with no subcategories the response is identical to before.
  * POST /categories gained an optional `parentCategoryId`, plus 404 PARENT_CATEGORY_NOT_FOUND and 400 SUBCATEGORY_DEPTH_EXCEEDED. A monthlyCap sent with a parent is a plain 400 VALIDATION_ERROR — caps are top-level-only.
  * 409 CATEGORY_NAME_ALREADY_EXISTS keeps its code but its meaning widened to 'unique case-insensitively WITHIN THE SAME PARENT'. Request 33 asserts that `Food > Snacks` and `Transport > Snacks` must BOTH succeed — that one is the proof that V6__categories_subcategories.sql landed, because V4's old single index forbade it.
  * PATCH /categories/{id} still has NO `parentCategoryId`. A row's level is fixed at creation; sending the key is ignored like any unknown field (request 42).

Settings gained `subcategoriesEnabled` (default false) — requests 15/16 assert three keys now, and request 43 toggles it. It is a UI AFFORDANCE that gates NOTHING server-side: POST accepts a parent whether it is on or off, GET /categories always returns the full tree, and turning it off writes one boolean and destroys nothing.

NOTE — the 403 PREMIUM_REQUIRED currency-gate requests that used to be in here are GONE. The currency selector became free on 2026-10-02 (docs/decisions/0017-per-currency-balances-and-partial-settlement.md §1); request 12 now asserts a plain 200 on a free account.

verification/reset tokens are NOT returned by the API by design — grab them from the app console, printed as [DEV EMAIL STUB], and paste into the verificationToken / resetToken variables.

NOTE — Domain 6 sub-steps 1 and 2 (Contacts + Groups), requests 113-142. Numbering continues from 112, which was the last request in the collection before these were appended. Seven endpoints: api-overview.md §6.1-§6.3 and §7.1-§7.4. SPLIT EXPENSES (§9) AND SETTLE UP (§10) ARE NOT IMPLEMENTED and have no requests here. Seven things to know before running them:
  * REQUESTS 113-115 CREATE AND LOG IN A SECOND ACCOUNT, and several later requests send that account's token instead of the usual one. The cross-user tests are not optional colour: the per-phone invite cooldown applies ACROSS ALL CALLERS (request 125) and the 404-not-403 membership rule can only be checked by a non-member (requests 139-141). Run 113-115 before anything else in this block.
  * NO REAL SMS IS SENT. LoggingSmsInviteGateway logs [DEV SMS STUB] with the number MASKED to its last four digits and reports success, exactly as LoggingEmailService does for email. A real provider is a new external dependency needing constitution §21 clearance. Watch the app console: the presence or ABSENCE of that line is the assertion for several requests.
  * FOUR LIMITS GUARD THE INVITE PATH, and they are not interchangeable. Per-phone cooldown (24h, across all callers — protects the recipient). Per-user cap (20 attempts per rolling 24h, counting failures — bounds cost). Plus TWO token buckets on POST /contacts/{id}/invite ONLY (a 5-per-10-min burst and a 60-per-24h cap), which deliberately do NOT apply to the implicit triggers, because a 429 there would fail a contact or group write because of an invite.
  * §6.2's inviteStatus ENUMERATION IS MISSING rate_limited, which §6.3 has. A cap-blocked invite on POST /contacts is therefore reported as cooldown_active — it never claims a send happened, and it is the only one of §6.2's four values meaning "not sent now, try later". Flagged to the System Architect in backend/README.md §15.6.
  * AUTHORIZATION IS MEMBERSHIP, NOT OWNERSHIP, for every §7 route. "Does created_by_user_id match the caller" is the WRONG test — a group row is legitimately shared. A non-member gets 404 GROUP_NOT_FOUND, NEVER 403, and byte-identically to a nonexistent id (requests 139/140): a 403 would confirm the group exists.
  * §7.4's CONTACT_NOT_FOUND IS A 400 WHILE §7.2's IS A 404. Requests 135 and 136 are that pair, run back to back. Both codes come from V10__groups.sql's own mapping table and are not interchangeable.
  * EVERY GROUP WRITE CREATES A 0.00 BALANCE ROW PER MEMBER, both registered and unregistered, via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET balance = balance + ? (relative deltas, never row locks — V10's CONCURRENCY block, option (b)). The service then asserts IN THE SAME TRANSACTION that every member has exactly one row and that the group's balances sum to zero. Request 142 carries the SQL to verify both by hand.

NOTE — Domain 7 (Activity log + Notifications), requests 165-187. Numbering continues from 164, which was the last request in the collection before these were appended. FOUR endpoints: api-overview.md §11.1, §12.1, §12.2 and §12.3 — the READ half of the two tables Domain 6 (requests 143-164) already WRITES. Eight things to know before running them:
  * RUN 143-164 FIRST. These requests create NO fixture of their own, deliberately: an activity describes a real event and a notification announces one, so there is nothing to seed and seeding either would put fabricated history in a user's feed. Every row these requests read was fanned out by the split save in 143 and the settlements in 155-159. An empty feed means those did not run.
  * ACTIVITIES GET A ROW FOR THE ACTOR TOO; NOTIFICATIONS GO TO EVERY OTHER AFFECTED MEMBER. Request 166 is the one that matters: account 2's feed holds the split it never touched — and it is produced by NO extra clause, because the fan-out wrote account 2 its OWN privately-owned row. The query is WHERE user_id = :caller and nothing else. That is the OPPOSITE of request 144's individual-balances read, where a user_id-only filter was the bug ADR 0023 §1 fixed; do not "fix" this one to look like that one.
  * ORDER BY THE DATE+TIME PAIR, NEVER created_at (V13 contract item 3), with `id` as the tie-break so the order is TOTAL and pagination is stable. Requests 172/173 are the proof: page 0 and page 1 at size 1 must be DISJOINT. Same-date-AND-time ties are the NORMAL case here, because one fan-out writes several rows from a single computed instant.
  * THE FOUR related_* FILTERS ARE NAVIGATION COLUMNS, and two of them behave in ways worth knowing (requests 167-170). transactionId matches AT MOST THE ACTOR'S ROW, because related_transaction_id is written only for the member whose personal transaction was created. contactId can match a contact THE READER DOES NOT OWN, which V13 explicitly sanctions. An unknown or other-user filter id is an EMPTY PAGE and never a 404 (request 171). There is NO settlementId filter, because there is no related_settlement_id column (V13 FLAG 1).
  * `read` IS THE ONLY MUTABLE COLUMN IN THIS ENTIRE DOMAIN. activities rows are immutable — §11 is one GET and nothing else — and neither table has a deleted_at or a version. There is no POST and no DELETE anywhere in §11 or §12.
  * *** THE updated_at BUMP IS THE ONE FAILURE THAT IS COMPLETELY INVISIBLE FROM THE API. *** §12.3's bulk UPDATE bypasses @UpdateTimestamp and this schema has NO trigger for updated_at on any table, so the statement sets it explicitly (V13 contract item 4) — exactly the trap that bit the category-rename propagation. Without it, a notification read on the phone stays unread on every other device forever, with no error anywhere. updated_at is NOT in §12.1's response shape, so SQL is the only check: backend/README.md §17.6 query 3.
  * §12.3 IS A PATCH, NOT A POST (request 185) — read from §12's own endpoint table rather than assumed. It writes only WHERE user_id = ? AND read = FALSE, so a second call affects zero rows and returns the identical 200 (request 187).
  * *** THE UNREAD BADGE HAS NO ENDPOINT. *** §12 defines three endpoints and none is a count, while ADR 0012 §4's 1-9 / "9+" badge renders on three screens (V13 FLAG 3). Request 176 shows the contract-supported route: GET /notifications?read=false&size=1 and read PageResponse.totalElements — correct, and indexed by idx_notifications_user_id_read. NEVER content.length, which is capped at the page size. A dedicated GET /notifications/unread-count is RECOMMENDED AND NOT BUILT (backend/README.md §17.5) — it needs no schema change and that same index already serves it, but inventing an endpoint the contract does not define is what constitution §15/§30 forbids.

NOTE — Domain 5 (Budget), requests 192-215. Numbering continues from 191, which was the last request in the collection before these were appended. THREE endpoints: api-overview.md §5.1, §5.2 and §5.3, against database/migrations/V14__budget.sql. Nine things to know before running them:
  * RUN 192 BEFORE 193, AND RUN BOTH ON AN ACCOUNT THAT HAS NEVER SAVED A BUDGET. 192 asserts 404 NO_ACTIVE_PERIOD, and once a period exists that answer can never come back for this account — budget_periods accumulates history and nothing deletes a row. Requests 193+ depend on foodCategoryId/transportCategoryId (request 19), subcategoryId (request 32) and otherAccessToken (request 115).
  * *** 404 NO_ACTIVE_PERIOD IS A NORMAL ANSWER, NOT AN ERROR. *** It is ADR 0011 post-auth routing signal, and after V14 applies it is the answer for EVERY existing account until it saves a period, because nothing is backfilled. Half of request 192 assertion is in the APP CONSOLE: there must be no log line for it.
  * *** THE ACTIVE PERIOD IS THE MOST RECENTLY CREATED ROW, NOT THE ONE COVERING TODAY, AND NOT THE ONE WITH THE LATEST END DATE. *** Request 203 discriminates between all three definitions at once, which is why the fixture dates look odd (a single-day 2026-10-15 period created LAST). It is also the live test for V14 FLAG 1, a contradiction inside data-model.md that the System Architect must resolve — the backend follows §3.1 / §5 intro / ADR 0011, not the Indexes section.
  * *** THE PERIOD RANGE IS INCLUSIVE ON BOTH ENDS. *** Requests 197 and 198 are the pair that proves it and must be run together: ONE shared day IS an overlap (400 PERIOD_OVERLAP), ADJACENT periods are NOT (201 Created). A failure in 198 is worse than a failure in 197 — it means a user cannot set up next month budget at all.
  * PERIOD_OVERLAP IS REACHABLE FROM A SCREEN THAT BELIEVES IT CANNOT HAPPEN (V14 FLAG 4, request 200). The frontend compares only against its single stored activePeriod; the server compares against ALL of the user periods. It must render as a real inline error on Budget Settings.
  * categoryCaps IS THE COMPLETE NEW SET ON EVERY SAVE, NEVER A DELTA (request 196). A category absent from the array has no cap for that period, so an edit REPLACES the cap rows — and omitting the key entirely CLEARS them, which is the correct reading of a PUT.
  * categoryName IS NEVER A REQUEST FIELD. The server resolves and snapshots it from categoryId at save time, fresh on every save (§5.2). A cap on a SUBCATEGORY is 400 VALIDATION_ERROR and never 404 (request 204) — it resolves and is owned by the caller, it is simply not eligible — and V14 deliberately does NOT enforce that structurally, so the service check is the only enforcement that exists.
  * *** A CAP SURVIVES ITS CATEGORY (requests 212-215). *** Deleting the capped category nulls the cap category_id and leaves the frozen name; it is NOT reassigned to Misc and NOT cascade-deleted (ADR 0021 §2.5). Neither does a RENAME touch a saved cap. Any test asserting otherwise is asserting the opposite of the specification.
  * V14 IS NEW AND NEEDS THE btree_gist EXTENSION. If the database role cannot create it, Flyway rolls the whole migration back and the backend does not boot — so a connection error on request 192 is more likely a failed migration than a bad token. V1 already creates pgcrypto against this same database, so the role is known to be able to.

NOTE — THE GROUP-MEMBERSHIP FIX ON POST/PATCH /transactions, requests 216-225. Numbering continues from 215. NO NEW ENDPOINT: these cover a BUG FIX to api-overview.md §4.2/§4.4, reported by the Project Owner and reproduced live. Six things to know:
  * THE BUG. POST /transactions with scope='group' returned 403 NOT_GROUP_MEMBER for EVERY input, even for a genuine member. Domain 4 was built before group_members existed, so §4.2's membership check was implemented as VACUOUSLY FALSE by construction. V10 is applied, so TransactionService now calls GroupMemberRepository.existsByGroupIdAndUserId per request, on BOTH write paths. Request 217 is the proof.
  * RUN 130 AND 138 FIRST (and 19 and 9). 216-225 create no group fixture of their own: 130 makes a group the first account IS in, 138 makes one it is NOT in, and both cases are needed.
  * THE CODE STAYS 403, AND AN UNKNOWN GROUP GETS THE SAME 403. §4.2's error table assigns this endpoint 403 explicitly and has no GROUP_NOT_FOUND row at all, and V10 contract item 1 records the divergence from §7's 404 convention as the approved contract. One membership query answers both halves, so nothing leaks — requests 219 and 220 must return IDENTICAL bodies. DO NOT "fix" either to a 404.
  * ONLY REGISTERED MEMBERSHIP COUNTS. The query matches group_members.user_id and deliberately NOT invited_contact_id: a contact placeholder has no account, so it can never be the authenticated caller.
  * fk_transactions_group_id (V10) MAPS TO 404 GROUP_NOT_FOUND AND IS THE RACE BACKSTOP, NOT THE ERROR PATH. The service pre-check resolves the group through group_members, so a nonexistent group is a 403 long before the FK sees it, and §7 has no group delete to open the window.
  * REQUEST 225 IS A KNOWN GAP, NOT A RULE: a group transaction cannot be demoted to scope='personal', because groupId on PATCH has no absent-vs-explicit-null distinction. Newly reachable, reachable from a screen, and it needs a Project Owner / System Architect decision. backend/README.md §13.12.

NOTE — ADR 0025 MULTIPLE PAYERS PER SPLIT EXPENSE (2026-11-06), requests 245-269. Numbering continues from 244. NO NEW ENDPOINT: POST /split-expenses gains an optional payers[] and SplitExpenseResponse gains payers[]. Four things to know:
  * V16__split_expense_payers.sql AND THIS BACKEND SHIP TOGETHER. Without V16 the backend does not boot (ddl-auto=validate).
  * RUN 113-164 FIRST (and 9, 19). These reuse groupId, unlinkedContactId, linkedByPhoneContactId, linkedByEmailContactId, plainContactId, individualBalanceId and groupSplitExpenseId. Request 254 creates one extra contact as account 2.
  * EXACTLY ONE PAYER FORM: legacy paidByUserId/paidByContactId OR payers[], never both (260) and never neither (261). The legacy form is NOT deprecated on the request. On the RESPONSE, paidBy* are deprecated: read payers[] (primary first, then amount desc).
  * BALANCES MOVE BY net = paid - share. 248, 253, 256 and 259 assert exact deltas against a value captured just before. The personal transaction is still the caller s SHARE, never what they paid (249).

item.name: 1. Register

exec: pm.test('201 Created', () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.test('emailVerified is false', () => pm.expect(b.emailVerified).to.eql(false));
pm.test('roles contains USER', () => pm.expect(b.roles).to.include('USER'));
pm.test('createdAt is present', () => pm.expect(b.createdAt).to.not.eql(null));
console.log('Now grab the [DEV EMAIL STUB] verification token from the app console.');
console.log('Domain 3: this registration also seeded 7 default categories inside the same transaction — request 19 checks them. Seven, not eight: ADR 0018 §2 dropped Income.');

item.name: 2. Login

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.collectionVariables.set('accessToken', b.accessToken);
pm.collectionVariables.set('refreshToken', b.refreshToken);
pm.test('expiresIn is 900', () => pm.expect(b.expiresIn).to.eql(900));
pm.test('user object present', () => pm.expect(b.user).to.be.an('object'));
console.log('Tokens saved to collection variables.');

item.name: 3. Refresh (rotates the token)

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.collectionVariables.set('accessToken', b.accessToken);
pm.collectionVariables.set('refreshToken', b.refreshToken);
pm.test('user omitted on refresh', () => pm.expect(b.user == null).to.be.true);
console.log('Rotated. Old token is now revoked — replay it to test reuse detection.');

item.name: 4. Logout

exec: pm.test('204 No Content', () => pm.response.to.have.status(204));

item.name: 5. Forgot password

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
console.log('Copy the [DEV EMAIL STUB] reset token from the app console into the resetToken variable.');

item.name: 6. Reset password
7. Verify email
8. Resend verification
Negative — wrong password (expect 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS)
Negative — anti-enumeration (unknown email, expect same 200 message)
Negative — replay old refresh token (expect REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED)
9. Get current user (Domain 2)

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.collectionVariables.set('userId', b.id);
pm.test('id present', () => pm.expect(b.id).to.be.a('string'));
pm.test('phone key present (may be null)', () => pm.expect(b).to.have.property('phone'));
pm.test('isPremium is a boolean', () => pm.expect(b.isPremium).to.be.a('boolean'));
pm.test('defaultCurrencyCode present', () => pm.expect(b.defaultCurrencyCode).to.be.a('string'));
pm.test('never leaks the password hash', () => pm.expect(b.passwordHash).to.be.undefined);
console.log('userId saved — use it for the user_settings and categories database checks.');

request.description: api-overview.md §2.1. Verify in the database that nothing was written — users.updated_at must be unchanged.

item.name: 10. Update current user — name + phone

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.test('firstName applied', () => pm.expect(b.firstName).to.eql('Janet'));
pm.test('phone applied', () => pm.expect(b.phone).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('phone')));
console.log('Check users.last_name is UNCHANGED — omitted fields must stay as they were.');

request.description: api-overview.md §2.2, partial update. lastName is deliberately omitted — verify it did not change.

item.name: 11. Update current user — clear phone (explicit null)

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.test('phone cleared', () => pm.expect(b.phone).to.eql(null));
console.log('Now send {} instead — phone must stay NULL, and nothing else may change either.');

if (b.some(c => c.name === 'Income')) { console.log('NOT A REGRESSION: this account was registered BEFORE ADR 0018, so it keeps a stray Income row. Nothing backfills or deletes it automatically — but since 2026-10-25 you CAN remove it through the API: DELETE /api/v1/categories/<that id> (request 90s shape). Or register a fresh account. ADR 0018, Existing data.'); }

if (b.length === 7) { console.log('SEVEN ROWS AND NO PROTECTED ONE MEANS V8__categories_misc_fallback.sql IS NOT APPLIED, or this account was registered against the pre-2026-10-25 catalog. Every request from 84 onwards will fail, and DELETE /categories/{id} answers 500 for this account, because the service RESOLVES the protected Misc row and deliberately never creates it (ADR 0021, Existing data). Apply V8 and register a fresh account.'); }

AND is_protected must be exactly 1 (V8s partial unique index uq_categories_user_protected guarantees at most one; its backfill plus the registration seed guarantee at least one).');

console.log('RESOLVED (was a FLAG here): the income-category identity question is answered by ADR 0018 — income is NOT a category. There is no Income row to find and no id to look up: an income transaction gets category_id = NULL plus the four server constants (Income / cash-outline / I / success, service/IncomeCategorySnapshot). The frontend deletes INCOME_CATEGORY_ID rather than re-pointing it (ADR 0018 §7).');

request.description:
api-overview.md §3.1, ADR 0018 §2, ADR 0021 §2.1. Run against a BRAND-NEW account: the 8 defaults are seeded inside the registration transaction, pre-Domain-3 accounts were deliberately not backfilled with the seven (they return only the Misc row V8 backfilled), and accounts registered between Domain 3 and ADR 0018 still carry a stray 'Income'.

The eight, IN SEED ORDER: Food/cafe-outline/F, Transport/car-outline/T, Groceries/cart-outline/G, Entertainment/film-outline/E, Home / Rent/home-outline/H, Shopping/bag-outline/S, Fitness / Leisure/barbell-outline/W, and — LAST, added 2026-10-25 — Misc/ellipsis-horizontal-outline/M. ('Fitness / Leisure' really does carry glyph W, not F — the frontend's own long-standing value.)

THE COUNT HAS MOVED 8 -> 7 -> 8, with different membership each time, and the second move is NOT the first one being undone. ADR 0018 removed `Income` because it was nonsense AS A CATEGORY (a user could tag an expense 'Income' or put a monthly SPENDING cap on it). ADR 0021 added `Misc`, which is an ordinary expense bucket a user can legitimately spend into — and it exists because DELETE /categories/{id} needs a reassignment target that is GUARANTEED to exist. It is the one row in the system with isProtected: true.

TWO-LEVEL TREE since 2026-10-22 (ADR 0019 §7): this array holds TOP-LEVEL categories only, and each entry carries its own children in `subcategories`. A subcategory NEVER appears at the root. For a fresh account that is invisible — all 8 are top-level with empty `subcategories`. Request 38 re-runs this once subcategories exist and asserts the nesting.

The seed set is unchanged by ADR 0019 §8: all rows top-level, and NO seeded subcategories (choosing which children 'Food' has is a product decision nobody has made, and seeding any would make the feature exist for users who never enabled it). Misc MAY receive subcategories like any other row; none is seeded.

This request saves foodCategoryId, transportCategoryId AND miscCategoryId — requests 32-42 need the first two (the same-name-under-two-parents case is what proves per-parent uniqueness landed), and requests 84-112 need the third.

request.description:
ADR 0018 §6: category names are unique CASE-INSENSITIVELY. 'pets' can no longer coexist with 'Pets' — two case-variant rows are indistinguishable in the picker and would give one category two separate monthly caps, silently doubling the user's intended limit.

The pre-request script lowercases {{categoryName}} into {{categoryNameLower}}, so this stays correct if you change the name variable. Requires request 20 to have created the original.

Two layers enforce this and both are deliberate (ADR 0018 §6): CategoryService's case-insensitive pre-check produces this clean 409, while the functional unique index uq_categories_user_id_lower_name (V4__categories_case_insensitive_name.sql) is the only real guard against two concurrent creates that both pass the pre-check. If that index were missing while the matcher expects it, the race loser would be a logged 500 instead of this 409.

Still whitespace-sensitive on purpose: names are trimmed service-side before both the check and storage.

Also worth trying through PATCH (request 23's shape): renaming a category onto another category's name in different case is also a 409 — but re-casing a category's OWN name ('Food' -> 'food' on the same id) is a legitimate 200, because the pre-check and the index both exclude the row being updated.

console.log('THIS IS THE REQUEST THAT PROVES V6__categories_subcategories.sql LANDED. A 409 here means the migration has not been applied: V4 s single index uq_categories_user_id_lower_name was unique on (user_id, lower(name)) across ALL rows, which forbids exactly this case. V6 drops it for two PARTIAL indexes, one per level.');

console.log('If this returns 409 while request 34 also returns 409, the backend half shipped against the old index. If it returns 500, the backend half did NOT ship and CategoryService is still matching V4 s name — the two halves must land in the same restart.');
console.log('DB CHECK: SELECT name, parent_category_id FROM categories WHERE user_id = <userId> AND lower(name) = lower(<subcategoryName>) returns TWO rows with different parents.');

request.description:
ADR 0019 §3. A name must be unique, case-insensitively, AMONG ITS SIBLINGS — not across the whole list. So 'Food > Snacks' and 'Transport > Snacks' may both exist, while 'Food' and 'food' still may not coexist at either level. Case-insensitivity was NOT relaxed; only the key's scope changed, from per-user to per-user-per-parent.

Server side this is two partial unique indexes replacing one:
  uq_categories_user_lower_name_top_level   (user_id, lower(name)) WHERE parent_category_id IS NULL
  uq_categories_user_parent_lower_name      (user_id, parent_category_id, lower(name)) WHERE parent_category_id IS NOT NULL
Both map to the SAME 409 CATEGORY_NAME_ALREADY_EXISTS code, so no client error mapping changes. They are PARTIAL rather than one three-column index because a plain unique key over a nullable column does not behave correctly in PostgreSQL — multiple NULLs do not conflict, so every top-level name would be exempt.

The relaxation gives back nothing the 2026-10-10 case-insensitivity decision won: two same-named leaves are distinguished BY THEIR PARENT (which the client must display — a bare 'Snacks' in a search result is the failure that decision exists to prevent), and they stay distinguishable in frozen history because `parentCategoryName` is snapshotted alongside `categoryName` once Domain 4 exists.

api-overview.md §4.1. The first PAGINATED endpoint in this API (constitution §11) — Domain 3's categories list is a plain array because its contract says so and the set is bounded.

Also try: ?type=income, ?type=expense, ?scope=personal, ?dateFrom=2026-10-01&dateTo=2026-10-31 (both bounds INCLUSIVE — put a row exactly on dateFrom and confirm it is included), and ?dateFrom=2026-12-01&dateTo=2026-01-01 (a reversed range is a legal EMPTY range, not a 400). ?scope=group is accepted and returns nothing until a group-scoped row exists — request 217 creates one, after which this filter matches it.

item.name: 50. Filter by the PARENT categoryId — THE ROLL-UP PROOF (expect 200)

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const b = pm.response.json();
const ids = b.content.map(t => t.id);
pm.test('includes the row tagged to the PARENT (request 45)', () => pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('transactionId')));
pm.test('ALSO includes the row tagged to its SUBCATEGORY (request 48) — this is the roll-up', () => pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('subcategoryTransactionId')));
pm.test('does NOT include the income row — a categoryId filter never matches income', () => pm.expect(ids).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('incomeTransactionId')));

console.log('ADR 0019 §5. A TOP-LEVEL categoryId matches transactions tagged to it AND to any of its subcategories, resolved from the categories table in a subquery inside the SAME statement — not from a denormalized column and not per row.');

console.log('An exact-match-only reading would make "Food spending" silently EXCLUDE Food > Snacks, which is the bug this behaviour exists to prevent. There is deliberately no includeSubcategories parameter — one documented behaviour.');
console.log('Income never matches because category_id IS NULL on every income row, and NULL satisfies neither the equality nor the IN. Use ?type=income for income (request 52).');

request.description:
api-overview.md §4.1's roll-up rule, data-model.md §2.2. Requires requests 45 and 48.

It is the same roll-up a parent's budget cap uses (§5.2): a parent's cap is evaluated INCLUSIVE of its children's spending, which is also why a subcategory may not carry a cap of its own.

item.name: 51. Filter by the SUBCATEGORY id — only its own row (the other half)

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const ids = pm.response.json().content.map(t => t.id);
pm.test('includes the subcategory s own row', () => pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('subcategoryTransactionId')));
pm.test('does NOT include the parent s row — a leaf id matches itself alone', () => pm.expect(ids).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('transactionId')));

console.log('THIS ASYMMETRY IS THE WHOLE BEHAVIOUR. A subcategory can have no children (exactly one level, ADR 0019 §2), so its id matches itself and nothing else — while its parent s id matches both. Run 50 and 51 together; either one alone proves nothing.');

console.log('ALSO CHECK, and it is a security check rather than a filter check: filter by ANOTHER ACCOUNT S category id (register a second account, use its category id here). Expect 200 with totalElements 0 and content [] — NOT a 404. §4.1 defines no error for this parameter, and a 404 would confirm to a non-owner that the id is real (security-architecture.md §2). A random non-existent UUID behaves identically.');

request.description: ADR 0019 §5: "a subcategory id matches that subcategory alone".

item.name: 52. Filter by type=income (expect 200)

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const rows = pm.response.json().content;
pm.test('every row is income', () => rows.forEach(t => pm.expect(t.type).to.eql('income')));
pm.test('every income row has categoryId null and categoryName Income', () => rows.forEach(t => { pm.expect(t.categoryId).to.eql(null); pm.expect(t.categoryName).to.eql('Income'); }));
pm.test('includes the row from request 47', () => pm.expect(rows.map(t => t.id)).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('incomeTransactionId')));
console.log('type is the SOLE discriminator between money in and money out, and always was (ADR 0018 §1) — which is exactly why no is_income/kind/slug column was ever added to categories.');

request.description: api-overview.md §4.1.

item.name: 53. Negative — list parameter validation (expect 400 VALIDATION_ERROR)

pm.test('VALIDATION_ERROR', () => pm.expect(b.error).to.eql('VALIDATION_ERROR'));
pm.test('fieldErrors names the offending parameter', () => pm.expect(b.fieldErrors).to.be.an('array').and.not.empty);

console.log('THIS USED TO BE A 500. GlobalExceptionHandler gained a BindException handler with Domain 4 — the first domain with validated QUERY parameters — and it is API-WIDE, so every later domain inherits it.');

console.log('If this returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with a logged stack trace, the thrown type is something other than BindException and one more @ExceptionHandler is needed. That is the one statically-unverifiable item in this area (backend/README.md §13.11 item 5).');

console.log('Also try each of these, all 400: ?size=0  ?size=101  ?size=100000  ?page=-1  ?type=Expense (capitalised — the vocabulary is exactly lowercase)  ?scope=team  ?dateFrom=24-10-2026  ?categoryId=not-a-uuid');
console.log('size is capped at 100 so one request cannot be made to read a whole table. That cap is DERIVED — the contract gives a default but no maximum (backend/README.md §13.10).');

request.description:
security-architecture.md §12.3 — Bean Validation on every DTO, in every domain, including the query DTO.

Injection hardening note: there is NO sort parameter on this endpoint. The contract defines none, so the ORDER BY is a literal in TransactionRepository and cannot be influenced from outside. If sorting is ever added it must map through a fixed allow-list, never pass a client string into an ORDER BY (§12.2).

item.name: 54. Get one transaction — premium enrichment (expect 200)

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.test('paymentMethodDisplay IS present here — §4.3 only', () => pm.expect(b).to.have.property('paymentMethodDisplay'));
pm.test('free tier: cash reads "Cash"', () => pm.expect(b.paymentMethodDisplay).to.eql('Cash'));
pm.test('paymentMethodUpiId is ABSENT — no users.upi_id column exists to source it from', () => pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property('paymentMethodUpiId'));
pm.test('receiptSignedUrl is ABSENT — the Cloudinary half is not implemented', () => pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property('receiptSignedUrl'));

console.log('PREMIUM CHECK: PATCH /users/me/premium {"isPremium": true} (request 17), then re-read the INCOME transaction from request 47 (paymentMode online). paymentMethodDisplay becomes "Unified Payments Interface". Flip premium off and it drops back to "Online".');

console.log('The gate is read from users.is_premium SERVER-SIDE, never from anything the client sends (security-architecture.md §2). A cash row is identical on both tiers (no online component to enrich) and a both row stays "Both" — §4.3 s table describes that premium cell as TWO ROWS the client composes from cashAmount/onlineAmount, specifying no single replacement string.');

console.log('paymentMethodUpiId NEEDS A DECISION: §4.3 sources it from the profile s UPI id, which today exists only as the frontend mock profileMocks.js#profileUser.mockUpiId. There is no users.upi_id column, and inventing one is what constitution §15/§30 forbids. Either the Database Architect adds a nullable column or the System Architect drops the field (backend/README.md §13.10).');

request.description:
api-overview.md §4.3. Confirm the two enrichment keys are ABSENT from request 49's list rows and from the 45/55 responses — "present only on this single-resource endpoint" is the contract's wording, enforced by field-level @JsonInclude(NON_NULL) on exactly those two components.

This is also the only endpoint in the whole API that may ever mint a receiptSignedUrl, and only AFTER its owner check has passed. That ordering is the access control (ADR 0020 §6): no endpoint may accept a publicId and return a URL for it.

item.name: 55. Update — title only (expect 200, version 2)

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.collectionVariables.set('transactionVersion', b.version);
pm.test('version incremented by exactly 1', () => pm.expect(b.version).to.eql(2));
pm.test('title changed', () => pm.expect(b.title).to.eql('Lunch at Saravana Bhavan'));
pm.test('categoryId UNCHANGED — a type-preserving patch that never touches categoryId never touches the snapshot', () => pm.expect(b.categoryId).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('foodCategoryId')));

console.log('DB CHECK: updated_at advanced, created_at did NOT, and every other column is untouched. V7 adds NO TRIGGER for version or updated_at — the application owns both, and updated_at is the confirmed last-write-wins column for sync (security-architecture.md §9).');

request.description: api-overview.md §4.4. Sending {"version": N} alone is a valid 200 that changes nothing but the version. Omitting version entirely is a 400 naming the field — it must never be read as 0, which is why the DTO field is Integer rather than int.

item.name: 56. Negative — replay a STALE version (expect 409 VERSION_CONFLICT)

exec: pm.collectionVariables.set('staleVersion', Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('transactionVersion')) - 1);
pm.test('409 Conflict', () => pm.response.to.have.status(409));
pm.test('VERSION_CONFLICT', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('VERSION_CONFLICT'));

console.log('DB CHECK, and it is the point of the two-phase write: NOTHING changed. SELECT title, version, updated_at FROM transactions WHERE id = <id> is identical to after request 55. The version check happens before a single field is mutated.');

console.log('TWO 409s LIVE ON THIS ENDPOINT WITH OPPOSITE CLIENT BEHAVIOUR. VERSION_CONFLICT means RE-FETCH AND RETRY. RECEIPT_ALREADY_ATTACHED (request 69) must NEVER be retried, because retrying re-sends the same reference. That is why they are separate codes — do not collapse them.');
console.log('The message deliberately does not state the current version: a client that needs it re-fetches the row, which is the action it has to take anyway.');

console.log('CONCURRENCY CHECK, the hardest item in this domain and the only one that proves the row lock works: fire TWO simultaneous PATCHes carrying the SAME version. Exactly one must get 200 and the other 409 — never two 200s. Without SELECT ... FOR UPDATE both would pass the comparison and one would silently overwrite the other.');

request.description:
api-overview.md §4.4's 409 VERSION_CONFLICT, security-architecture.md §9.

Implemented as a plain version column plus a row lock rather than a JPA @Version field — see Transaction#version's Javadoc and backend/README.md §13.8 for why (the contract pins the initial value at 1, and this project's assigned-id entities go through merge rather than persist, which makes a @Version seed's behaviour something that could not be verified without running it).

item.name: 57. Update — set notes (expect 200)

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.collectionVariables.set('transactionVersion', b.version);
pm.test('notes set', () => pm.expect(b.notes).to.eql('split with Rahul, settled in cash'));

request.description:
Requests 57-59 are the absent-vs-explicit-null trio, and they must be run in order. notes is stored exactly as sent — NOT trimmed, unlike title: it is free text where whitespace may be deliberate, and clearing is expressed by an explicit null rather than by a blank string.

notes has no length limit, at the Database Architect's explicit instruction (the column is uncapped `text`) and because the contract gives none. It is the one unbounded request field in this domain — flagged honestly in backend/README.md §13.10.

item.name: 58. Update — omitted notes must stay UNCHANGED (expect 200)

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.collectionVariables.set('transactionVersion', b.version);
pm.test('notes UNCHANGED — the key was absent', () => pm.expect(b.notes).to.eql('split with Rahul, settled in cash'));
pm.test('title changed', () => pm.expect(b.title).to.eql('Lunch'));

request.description: The notes key is simply ABSENT here. Compare with request 59, which sends it explicitly as null.

item.name: 59. Update — CLEAR notes with an explicit null (expect 200)

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.collectionVariables.set('transactionVersion', b.version);
pm.test('notes CLEARED', () => pm.expect(b.notes).to.eql(null));
console.log('DB CHECK: notes IS NULL. Requests 58 and 59 MUST NOT behave the same way — that distinction is the whole reason UpdateTransactionRequest is a class rather than a record.');

console.log('The mechanism is COPIED from UpdateUserRequest/UpdateCategoryRequest, not reinvented (backend/README.md §11.7 §12.4): Jackson calls a setter only for a property physically present in the JSON, so hasNotes() means exactly "the client sent a notes key", independent of its value. Only notes and receiptPublicId carry presence flags — every other field here needs only its value.');

request.description: api-overview.md §4.4: "an absent field leaves the column unchanged; an explicit null clears it" — §3.3's verified monthlyCap convention applied unchanged, so no new convention is invented and one request object does not end up carrying two.

item.name: 60. Update — expense -> income (expect 200, all five snapshot values overwritten)

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

pm.test('categoryId nulled by the SERVER', () => pm.expect(b.categoryId).to.eql(null));

console.log('ADR 0018 §3.3 — getting either type transition wrong leaves a row NOTHING IN THE SYSTEM CAN RENDER CORRECTLY OR EXPLAIN. All five move together or none do: CategorySnapshot.applyTo makes a partial application structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged.');
console.log('Also try adding "categoryId": "<any>" to this same request — 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.');

item.name: 61. Negative — income -> expense WITHOUT categoryId (expect 400)

exec: pm.test('400 Bad Request', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));
pm.test('VALIDATION_ERROR', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('VALIDATION_ERROR'));

console.log('§4.4: on income -> expense, categoryId becomes REQUIRED IN THAT SAME REQUEST. Without this rule the row would be left with type=expense, category_id = NULL and category_name = Income — a state nothing could render correctly or explain.');
console.log('DB CHECK: still type = income, version UNCHANGED. The rejection is decided before anything is mutated.');

console.log('NOTE the database is NOT backstopping this. CHECK ((type = expense) = (category_id IS NOT NULL)) could not be added — it would make category_id s own ON DELETE SET NULL unexecutable, since the cascade s UPDATE would violate it. CategorySnapshotResolver is the ONLY enforcement that exists.');

item.name: 62. Update — income -> expense WITH categoryId (expect 200)

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.collectionVariables.set('transactionVersion', b.version);
pm.test('categoryId now set', () => pm.expect(b.categoryId).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('transportCategoryId')));
pm.test('snapshot re-derived from the resolved category', () => pm.expect(b.categoryName).to.not.eql('Income'));
pm.test('categoryTone back to neutral', () => pm.expect(b.categoryTone).to.eql('neutral'));
pm.test('parentCategoryName null — Transport is top-level', () => pm.expect(b.parentCategoryName).to.eql(null));
console.log('TWO MORE PATCH CASES WORTH RUNNING BY HAND, both on the row from request 48 (tagged to a SUBCATEGORY):');

console.log('  (d1) patch only its amount -> categoryId, categoryName and parentCategoryName are ALL unchanged. That is what makes editing a transaction without opening the category picker preserve the subcategory assignment.');
console.log('  (d2) then patch its categoryId to a TOP-LEVEL category -> parentCategoryName is reset to NULL. All five are re-derived together, never partially.');

console.log('A third case the contract implies and the implementation respects: if a category is ever DELETED, ON DELETE SET NULL leaves a legitimate expense with category_id NULL and intact snapshot values. A PATCH that does not touch categoryId must NOT demand one for such a row — which is why the snapshot is re-derived only when type changes or a categoryId is supplied.');

item.name: 63. Negative — paymentMode 'both' with a wrong sum (expect 400)

exec: pm.test('400 Bad Request', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));
pm.test('VALIDATION_ERROR', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('VALIDATION_ERROR'));

console.log('security-architecture.md §3: the client s IDENTICAL check is UX ONLY and is never trusted. Compared with BigDecimal.compareTo — exact decimal, scale insensitive — over values already constrained to at most two decimal places by @Digits, which is STRICTER than §3 s "round to integer paise before comparing" rather than an approximation of it. chk_transactions_cash_online_sum compares exactly too.');

console.log('Also 400: "amount": 10.005 (three decimal places — the sub-paise guard), and a NEGATIVE cashAmount. A ZERO portion is allowed: it is arithmetically legal, while -100 and 350 would "sum correctly" to 250 and record nonsense (backend/README.md §13.10).');

pm.collectionVariables.set('transactionVersion', b.version);

The stored portions no longer add up, and the server will not guess how to redistribute someone s money. The client must send a consistent triple, which is what keeps the row s arithmetic true at every instant.');

api-overview.md §4.2/§4.4.

payment_mode is NOT NULL on every row regardless of user_settings.payment_mode_enabled — that flag decides whether Add Expense SHOWS the fields, never whether the column is populated. Nothing in this write path reads that setting.

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

pm.collectionVariables.set('transactionVersion', b.version);
pm.test('paymentMode cash', () => pm.expect(b.paymentMode).to.eql('cash'));

The client did NOT have to null out the portions it was abandoning — but STATING one alongside a single mode IS contradictory and is a 400: try {"version": <next>, "paymentMode": "cash", "cashAmount": 50}. An explicit "cashAmount": null is fine, so a client that always sends every key is unaffected.');

request.description: api-overview.md §4.4.

item.name: 66. txnTime is FROZEN — sending it is ignored (expect 200, unchanged)

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.collectionVariables.set('transactionVersion', b.version);
pm.test('txnTime UNCHANGED — still 13:45', () => pm.expect(b.txnTime).to.eql('13:45'));
pm.test('txnDate DID change — that one is updatable', () => pm.expect(b.txnDate).to.eql('2026-10-25'));

console.log('The refusal is STRUCTURAL rather than a check someone has to remember: there is no txnTime field on the request DTO, Transaction.txnTime is mapped @Column(updatable = false), and no code path writes it on update. So the key is ignored exactly as any unknown field is — the same shape ADR 0019 §9 chose for reparenting a category.');
console.log('DB CHECK: SELECT txn_time FROM transactions WHERE id = <id> — unchanged.');

request.description: txn_time must travel from the client at CREATION because the true creation moment may occur offline, long before the write reaches the server (data-model.md §2.2) — but it is never re-stamped.

item.name: 67. Negative — scope 'group' with an UNKNOWN groupId (expect 403 NOT_GROUP_MEMBER)

exec: pm.test('403 Forbidden', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));
pm.test('NOT_GROUP_MEMBER', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('NOT_GROUP_MEMBER'));

console.log('*** UPDATED 2026-11-03 — THIS REQUEST STILL PASSES, BUT IT NOW TESTS SOMETHING NARROWER. *** It used to be the proof that EVERY scope=group write was refused, because group_members did not exist and §4.2 check was VACUOUSLY FALSE for every input. That was a bug for real members and is FIXED. The hardcoded groupId here names no group, so the answer is unchanged: an unknown group gets the same 403 NOT_GROUP_MEMBER as a real group the caller is not in. Requests 216-225 are the full matrix, including the 201 a member now gets.');

console.log('The 404-not-403 convention is not violated: the resource being addressed is the caller s own NEW transaction, groupId is an INPUT to that write, and §4.2 s error table assigns it this code explicitly. DO NOT FIX THIS TO 404 — V10 contract item 1 records the divergence from §7 404 convention as the approved contract.');

console.log('ALSO 400 (not 403): scope "group" with NO groupId — the contract s "required iff", answered first because it is cheap and depends on nothing. AND: a groupId with scope "personal" — the other direction of the same iff, which the database also refuses via chk_transactions_group_id_matches_scope. Requests 221 and 222.');

console.log('DB CHECK after all of Domain 4 and BEFORE request 217: SELECT count(*) FROM transactions WHERE group_id IS NOT NULL; -> 0. After 217 it is 1. split_expense_id stays 0 here — only a split expense can set it (§9.1 does, on its own consumption-share row). Both columns exist in V7 and are mapped, so the response values are genuine reads rather than hardcoded nulls; both FOREIGN KEYS now exist, in V10 and V11.');

request.description:
api-overview.md §4.2's 403 NOT_GROUP_MEMBER row.

Worth knowing, because the shipped frontend relies on it: an INDIVIDUAL split's consumption-share row is scope='personal' with groupId: null. "Came from a split" is NOT the same thing as "group-scoped".

item.name: 68. Receipt — claim a valid publicId (expect 200)

exec: pm.collectionVariables.set('receiptPublicId', 'myexpense/receipts/' + pm.collectionVariables.get('userId') + '/pm-test-001');
pm.collectionVariables.set('foreignReceiptPublicId', 'myexpense/receipts/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/pm-test-002');
pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.collectionVariables.set('transactionVersion', b.version);
pm.test('receiptPublicId stored verbatim', () => pm.expect(b.receiptPublicId).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('receiptPublicId')));
pm.test('it is NOT a URL and carries no signed URL alongside it', () => pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property('receiptSignedUrl'));

console.log('Requires request 9 to have run (it saves userId). HAND-MADE on purpose: POST /receipts/upload-signature is not implemented, so constructing one is the only way to get a value today — and that is exactly how the claim check is tested.');

console.log('THE CLAIM CHECK (ADR 0020 §3) is the only server-side validation of this field and the one that matters: the value must match the configured root AND carry the caller s OWN user id. Shape: {app.receipts.public-id-root}/receipts/{callerUserId}/{assetName}. Default root `myexpense`, overridable with RECEIPT_PUBLIC_ID_ROOT — a FOLDER NAME, not a secret, which is why it has a default.');

console.log('EXISTENCE IS DELIBERATELY NOT VERIFIED. The server does not call Cloudinary: that would put a third-party round trip on a financial write path, it proves nothing for a write arriving later through /sync/push, and the failure it would catch is a broken thumbnail on the claimant s OWN row, not a security failure.');
console.log('NOW RUN THESE FOUR 400s by hand, each a different way to fail the check:');
console.log('  myexpense/receipts/<ANOTHER userId>/abc  (someone else s folder — the one that actually matters)');
console.log('  receipts/<YOUR userId>/abc               (no root)');
console.log('  myexpense/receipts/<YOUR userId>/sub/abc (a DEEPER path — this is what stops a crafted value pointing at a folder the signature was never issued for)');
console.log('  myexpense/receipts/<YOUR userId>/        (empty asset name)');

request.description:
api-overview.md §4.2 rule 3 / §4.4, ADR 0020 §3.

receiptPublicId holds a Cloudinary public_id and is NOT a URL: it cannot be navigated to, rendered, or handed to an Image component. A list row can tell THAT a receipt exists from this field being non-null without being handed the means to read it. Reading the asset needs a short-lived signed delivery URL that only GET /transactions/{id} may mint — and that half is not implemented (backend/README.md §13.9).

item.name: 69. Negative — a SECOND transaction claiming the same receipt (expect 409)

exec: pm.test('409 Conflict', () => pm.response.to.have.status(409));
pm.test('RECEIPT_ALREADY_ATTACHED, NOT VERSION_CONFLICT', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('RECEIPT_ALREADY_ATTACHED'));
console.log('ONE ASSET, ONE TRANSACTION (ADR 0020 §3). Without it, removing or replacing one transaction s receipt could later destroy or orphan an asset another row still renders.');

console.log('NOT RETRYABLE — and that is the whole reason it has its own code rather than sharing VERSION_CONFLICT s. Retrying re-sends the same reference and will fail identically forever; the correct client behaviour is to obtain a fresh signature and upload again, the OPPOSITE of re-fetch-and-retry.');

console.log('Re-sending a transaction s OWN current receiptPublicId on PATCH is NOT a conflict (the pre-check excludes that row) — confirm by re-running request 68.');

A parent amount is INCLUSIVE of its children - the same roll-up GET /transactions?categoryId=<FOOD id> and a parent budget cap already use. THREE SURFACES, ONE DEFINITION of spending in this category; if they ever disagree, a user sees a pie slice that contradicts their budget warning.');

request.description:
api-overview.md §3.4, ADR 0021 §2.3/§2.4. No request body.

One database transaction, in this order: resolve the target owner-scoped (404 if not the caller's), refuse the protected row (400), resolve the reassignment target BY COLUMN, resolve the affected id set (the target plus its subcategory ids), ONE UPDATE reassigning every transaction in that set, then DELETE the subcategory rows and finally the target row.

Every answer a client can be given is decided BEFORE the first write, which is why no noRollbackFor is needed anywhere in this domain — the one thing that can still throw after the UPDATE is an invariant failure, and there a rollback is exactly what must happen.

console.log('CHECK 1 — ONE BALANCE ROW PER MEMBER, BOTH KINDS: SELECT id, user_id, invited_contact_id, balance FROM group_member_balances WHERE group_id = <groupId>; — expect FOUR rows, every balance 0.00, and at least one row carrying invited_contact_id with user_id NULL. *** THAT LAST ROW IS WHAT ADR 0023 §2 S RESHAPE EXISTS FOR: before it, group_member_balances had a composite PK (group_id, user_id) with user_id NOT NULL, so an UNREGISTERED member s share had nowhere to land at all. ***');

console.log('CHECK 2 — ZERO-SUM (V10 s CONCURRENCY block): SELECT b.group_id, sum(b.balance) AS net FROM group_member_balances AS b GROUP BY b.group_id HAVING sum(b.balance) <> 0; — *** THIS MUST RETURN NO ROWS, FOR EVERY GROUP, ALWAYS. *** A non-zero sum means a lost update, a missed member, or a settlement applied to one side only.');

console.log('WHY BOTH CHECKS, AND NOT JUST ZERO-SUM: while every balance is 0.00, A SUM OVER FEWER ROWS IS STILL ZERO — so zero-sum ALONE CANNOT DETECT A MISSED MEMBER in this sub-step. The service runs both, in the same transaction, and a violation THROWS and rolls the write back — which is the intended outcome, and the one place in this domain where noRollbackFor would be actively wrong.');

console.log('THE SERIALISATION MECHANISM IS RELATIVE DELTAS, DELIBERATELY CHOSEN (V10 s CONCURRENCY block, option (b)): INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (group_id, user_id) DO UPDATE SET balance = group_member_balances.balance + excluded.balance. SELECT ... FOR UPDATE is NOT used anywhere on this table and must not be added — V10 warns against mixing the two. A delta REMOVES the read-modify-write cycle rather than guarding it, and it is the shape partial settlement (ADR 0023 §4) already needs.');

console.log('TWO UPSERT STATEMENTS, ONE PER MEMBER KIND, AND THEY CANNOT BE MERGED: an ON CONFLICT clause names exactly ONE inference target, and a registered member s row can only collide on (group_id, user_id) while a placeholder s can only collide on (group_id, invited_contact_id). item.name: 164. *** THE LESSER-POSITION BOUND *** — a group settlement above min(|debtor|, creditor)

It is ADR 0017 §4 s \"rejected, never clamped, never sign-flipped\" rule applied to TWO rows instead of one.');

console.log('THE BOUND IS NEVER COMPUTED AS A min() THAT GETS WRITTEN. Each side s own guard lives inside its own UPDATE — balance >= :amount for the creditor, balance <= -:amount for the debtor — and the CONJUNCTION of the two IS amount <= min(|debtor|, creditor). Expressing it that way is what makes it race-safe: a pre-computed minimum is a READ, and V12 contract item 3 is explicit that this read must be serialised against a concurrent settle. The service s pre-read produces this clean 400; the predicates are what cannot be raced.');

console.log('BOTH SIDES OR NEITHER. If the first bounded UPDATE had succeeded and the second matched zero rows, the whole transaction ROLLS BACK — a settlement that moved one side and not the other would break the zero-sum invariant permanently, in the one table whose entire purpose is to be independently verifiable by both parties later. That is the one place in this domain where a rollback is REQUIRED rather than merely acceptable, and it is why no noRollbackFor appears anywhere here.');

Here the opposite is true: N rows, one reader each, and user_id IS the correct authorization test (V13 says so explicitly, calling out that this is unlike V10/V11 s tables). ADR 0008 §2.2 s four templates are VIEWER-RELATIVE: the payer reads "You paid 500 to <name> for ..." and everyone else reads "<name> paid 500 to you for ...". item.name: 188. *** DATE-RANGE REGRESSION *** GET /transactions?dateFrom= — 200, NOT 500 (§4.1)

PostgreSQL rejected the statement at PARSE time with "could not determine data type of parameter $6", because (:dateFrom is null or t.txnDate >= :dateFrom) emits the parameter as TWO placeholders and the one inside is null has no type context — which only date/time parameters cannot survive, since the JDBC driver binds them with an unspecified type OID on purpose. Fixed by t.txnDate >= coalesce(:dateFrom, t.txnDate). backend/README.md §13.11 item 1 has the full record.');

console.log('IF THIS IS A 500 AGAIN, the coalesce form has been reverted to the (:param is null or ...) idiom. NEVER put a LocalDate, LocalTime, OffsetDateTime or Instant parameter inside an is null check. The idiom is still correct for UUID, String, numeric, boolean and converter-backed enum parameters — which is why ?type=, ?scope= and ?categoryId= never failed.');

console.log('CROSS-CHECK THE BOUND IS INCLUSIVE AND NOT WIDENED: run the same call with no dates. totalElements there must be >= the number here, and every row missing from this page must have a txnDate strictly before 2026-09-01.');
